current_affairs.title: Cabinet approves conferring status of Classical Language to Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese and Bengali languages
current_affairs.gsCategory: GS Paper I (Indian Heritage, Culture & Languages)
current_affairs.summary: The Union Cabinet chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi conferred the status of Classical Language to five languages: Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese, and Bengali, expanding the roster from six to eleven recognized classical languages.
prelimsPointers: Criteria established in 2004/2005: High antiquity of early texts/recorded history over 1500-2000 years, valuable body of ancient literature, original literary tradition, distinct from modern forms
Linguistic Experts Committee (LEC) under Ministry of Culture (Sahitya Akademi) examines proposals
Total Classical Languages in India now 11: Tamil (2004), Sanskrit (2005), Telugu (2008), Kannada (2008), Malayalam (2013), Odia (2014), plus Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese, and Bengali (2024)
current_affairs.mainsRelevance: GS-1 Indian Culture: Preservation of ancient linguistic heritage, linguistic diversity, promotion of academic research chairs, and international recognition of indigenous literatures.

current_affairs.title: Cabinet accepts recommendations of High-Level Committee on Simultaneous Elections
current_affairs.sourceName: Cabinet / Ministry of Law and Justice
current_affairs.summary: The Union Cabinet accepted the recommendations of the High-Level Committee on Simultaneous Elections chaired by former President Ram Nath Kovind, recommending a phased approach to synchronize elections across all tiers of Indian democracy.
prelimsPointers: Phase 1 proposes simultaneous elections for Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies
Phase 2 synchronizes local bodies (Municipalities and Panchayats) within 100 days of general elections
Recommendation of a single common electoral roll and Electoral Photo Identity Card (EPIC) across Union, State, and local bodies
current_affairs.mainsRelevance: GS-2 Constitutional Architecture: Federalism vs governance efficiency, impact of election cycles on policy paralysis, Model Code of Conduct, and constitutional amendments required (Articles 83, 172, 324A).

current_affairs.title: Cabinet approves Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Unnat Gram Abhiyan
current_affairs.gsCategory: GS Paper II (Welfare Schemes & Vulnerable Sections)
current_affairs.summary: The Union Cabinet approved the Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Unnat Gram Abhiyan with a total outlay of Rs.79,156 crore (Central share: Rs.56,333 crore; State share: Rs.22,823 crore) to ensure saturation of critical infrastructure and services for over 5 crore tribal people.
prelimsPointers: Covers ~63,000 tribal-majority villages across 549 districts and 2,740 blocks in 30 States/UTs
Encompasses 25 interventions implemented by 17 line ministries coordinated through Development Action Plan for Scheduled Tribes (DAPST)
Focuses on pucca houses (PMAY-G), piped water supply (JJM), solar lighting, forest rights (FRA) support, and livelihood training
current_affairs.mainsRelevance: GS-2 Social Justice: Targeted tribal development, inter-ministerial convergence mechanisms, reducing socio-economic disparities in Fifth and Sixth Schedule areas, and bridging critical infrastructural deficits.

current_affairs.title: Cabinet approves Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Urban 2.0 Scheme
current_affairs.sourceName: Cabinet / Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
current_affairs.gsCategory: GS Paper II (Governance, Urbanization & Social Welfare)
current_affairs.summary: The Union Cabinet approved the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Urban (PMAY-U) 2.0 scheme with financial assistance to 1 crore urban poor and middle-class families to construct, purchase, or rent affordable houses with an investment of Rs.10 lakh crore.
prelimsPointers: Government assistance/subsidy component of Rs.2.30 lakh crore over 5 years
Four verticals: Beneficiary-Led Construction (BLC), Affordable Housing in Partnership (AHP), Affordable Rental Housing (ARH), and Interest Subsidy Scheme (ISS)
Eligibility includes Economically Weaker Section (EWS), Low Income Group (LIG), and Middle Income Group (MIG) families not owning a pucca house
current_affairs.mainsRelevance: GS-2 Governance & GS-1 Urbanization: Rapid urban migration, slum redevelopment, inclusive urban housing infrastructure, and cooperative federalism in municipal delivery.

current_affairs.title: Cabinet approves 'Mission Mausam' to create a more weather-ready and climate-smart Bharat with an outlay of Rs.2,000 crore over two years
current_affairs.gsCategory: GS Paper III (Science & Technology / Disaster Management)
current_affairs.summary: The Union Cabinet approved 'Mission Mausam' with an outlay of Rs.2,000 crore over two years to build a climate-smart Bharat by drastically enhancing weather observation networks, supercomputing infrastructure, and cloud-physics research.
prelimsPointers: Nodal Ministry: Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES)
Implemented by three premier institutes: India Meteorological Department (IMD), Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM), and National Centre for Medium Range Weather Forecasting (NCMRWF)
Deploys next-generation Doppler radars, high-resolution satellite payloads, advanced atmospheric laboratories, and AI/ML predictive modeling
current_affairs.mainsRelevance: GS-3 Disaster Management & Science: Early warning systems for extreme weather events (cyclones, cloudbursts, heatwaves), agricultural climate resilience, and economic loss mitigation.

current_affairs.title: Union Cabinet approves 'BioE3 (Biotechnology for Economy, Environment and Employment) Policy for Fostering High Performance Biomanufacturing' of Department of Biotechnology
current_affairs.sourceName: Cabinet / Ministry of Science and Technology
current_affairs.gsCategory: GS Paper III (Science & Technology / Biotechnology & Environment)
current_affairs.summary: The Union Cabinet approved the landmark BioE3 Policy to foster high-performance biomanufacturing, aiming to pivot India from chemical-based industrial manufacturing to sustainable, biologically-driven manufacturing models.
prelimsPointers: Six thematic areas: High-value bio-based chemicals/biopolymers, Smart proteins & functional foods, Precision biotherapeutics, Climate-resilient agriculture, Carbon capture & utilization, Marine and space research
Establishes institutional Biomanufacturing Hubs, Biofoundries, and Bio-AI Hubs across India
Directly aligns with India's international commitment of Net-Zero carbon emissions by 2070
current_affairs.mainsRelevance: GS-3 Science & Tech: Industrial biotechnology indigenization, circular bioeconomy transition, bio-based employment creation, and green industrial policies.

current_affairs.title: Cabinet approves PM-Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana for installing rooftop solar in One Crore households
current_affairs.sourceName: Cabinet / Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
current_affairs.summary: The Union Cabinet approved the PM-Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana with a massive financial outlay of Rs.75,021 crore to provide up to 300 units of free electricity per month for 1 crore households through rooftop solar systems.
prelimsPointers: Central Financial Assistance (CFA): Rs.30,000 per kW for up to 2 kW systems; Rs.18,000 per kW for additional 1 kW capacity (max Rs.78,000 for 3 kW+)
Target: 30 GW rooftop solar capacity addition, resulting in reduction of 720 million tonnes of CO2 equivalent emissions over 25-year lifetime
Includes development of a 'Model Solar Village' in each district and collateral-free low-interest loan products (~7% interest)
current_affairs.mainsRelevance: GS-3 Energy Infrastructure: DISCOM turnaround through decentralized generation, solar manufacturing supply chains, democratization of power generation, and INDC climate targets.

current_affairs.title: Union Cabinet approves establishment of Rs.1,000 crore Venture Capital Fund for Space Sector under aegis of IN-SPACe
current_affairs.gsCategory: GS Paper III (Science & Technology / Space Economy)
current_affairs.summary: The Union Cabinet approved the creation of a dedicated Rs.1,000 crore Venture Capital Fund managed under the aegis of IN-SPACe to provide growth-stage risk equity capital to Indian space tech startups.
prelimsPointers: Nodal Agency: IN-SPACe (Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre)
Deployment period: Up to 5 years, investing an average of Rs.150–250 crore annually across approximately 40 space startups
Investment size: Growth stage (Rs.10–30 crore) and Late-growth stage (Rs.30–60 crore)
current_affairs.mainsRelevance: GS-3 Technology & Economy: Commercialization of Indian space industry, preventing brain-drain and external domiciling of Indian spacetech IP, and scaling India's share in global space economy towards 10%.

current_affairs.title: Launch of National Mission on Natural Farming
current_affairs.sourceName: Cabinet / Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
current_affairs.summary: The Union Cabinet approved the launch of the National Mission on Natural Farming (NMNF) as a standalone Centrally Sponsored Scheme with an outlay of Rs.2,481 crore to promote chemical-free, ecosystem-based farming across India.
prelimsPointers: Total outlay of Rs.2,481 crore (Central share: Rs.1,584 crore; State share: Rs.897 crore) up to 2025-26
Targets establishing 15,000 natural farming clusters covering 7.5 lakh hectares and 10,000 Bio-input Resource Centres (BRCs)
Deploys Community Resource Persons (CRPs)/Krishi Sakhis and establishes a single national brand and easy certification system
current_affairs.mainsRelevance: GS-3 Agriculture: Soil health restoration, chemical fertilizer subsidy reduction, climate-resilient organic agriculture, and lowering input costs for small and marginal farmers.

mcqs.question:
With reference to the Right to Equality under Article 14 of the Indian Constitution, consider the following statements:
1. 'Equality before the Law' is of British origin and is a negative concept.
2. 'Equal Protection of the Laws' is of American origin and is a positive concept.
3. The Supreme Court held that the 'Rule of Law' embodied in Article 14 is a basic feature of the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.explanation: All three statements are correct. Statement 1 is correct as 'Equality before law' is taken from the British legal system (absence of special privileges). Statement 2 is correct as 'Equal protection of laws' is from the American Constitution (equality of treatment under equal circumstances). Statement 3 is correct as the Supreme Court has declared Rule of Law as part of the Basic Structure doctrine.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following categories of Fundamental Rights incorporates protection against untouchability as a form of discrimination?
mcqs.explanation: Article 17 abolishes 'untouchability' and forbids its practice in any form. It is placed under the heading 'Right to Equality' (Articles 14 to 18) in Part III of the Constitution.
